chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Preparing for record dates and learning the chords
summary: He recorded the tune once before with little arrangement; record dates often give too little time to learn a solo, and knowing chords and melody is important.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: That's not the only time that tune was recorded, though, is it?
I recorded it once, oh, with Lem Davis years ago.
That's it. I've got that one. That's on Savoy.

Yeah, but that wasn't a very good one. This is a better one. I had some sort of an arrangement on this time. That other one, there wasn't no arrangement on it. It just was like a solo, so... And the guys weren't familiar with the chords and things. So it was...
Does that happen often on record dates, that you don't have enough time to really familiarize yourself with a tune and stuff?
Was it that way earlier, too? Or did they prepare more for it then?

They used to have rehearsals. But sometimes you'd get a solo right at the recording date, and you really didn't have it down like you should have had. You should have had more time to study it if you had a solo; to study
it and get your chords right.
It's important that you know that, so you can...
It's very important that you know the chords. And then you're familiar with the lead of the number, you're familiar with the...
